Brit Indie 26

Reading too much into Music Week's 'Industry Leaders Hopes for 2026'

‘Britainicana’ & The rise of Country music in the UK

ANNA-SOPHIE MERTENS

LIVE NATION

“I’d like more growth in the UK’s country and Americana scene, which has really taken off in the last few years. I’m particularly excited about the first edition of State Fayre, our new weekend camping festival celebrating all things rock, Americana and barbecue. It brings something new to the UK festival landscape.”

Country music has been booming in popularity in the UK for a few years now. The UK Country Music Association reported that in 2025, ‘the growth of country music consumption in the UK was the fastest of anywhere in the world… 2x faster than the overall market’. Much of that growth is driven by massive US country pop artists like Zach Bryan, who sold out 2 nights at Hyde Park last June, but there is a steadily growing wave of British & Irish country music artists breaking into the country music charts – Scottish singer-songwriter Rianne Downey held the number one spot for 3 weeks with her album ‘The Consequence of Love’, the group First Time Flyers reached number one in September, and the Northern Irish artist Gareth regularly features in the top 40 of weekly country radio airplay charts. Myles Smith is more country-adjacent than straightforward country, but he had another huge year - winning the BRITs Rising Star award for 2025, selling out his headline tour and remaining consistenly among the top artists played on the radio throughout the year.

As Anna-Sophie Mertens, senior promoter at Live Nation, makes clear: country music is big business in the UK at the moment. Folky singer-songwriters like Taylor Swift or Ed Sheeran have always been hugely popular and succesful here, but the enormous success of Americana artists like Zack Bryan, Shaboozey and Morgan Wallen feels like something new - I don’t think songs like Morgan Wallen’s ‘What I Want’, or Bryan’s ‘Plastic Cigarette’ would have broken through in the same way just a few years ago.
